family.tagline: Cut flowers, a new baby, and an order list on the shelf.
family.story: Ren grows cut flowers for the Saturday market and a flower-share list. Kemi designs for clients from a glass nook beside the beds. Their baby, Haru, sleeps through most of it.

companion.name: Hana
companion.job: Opens HortusFox in its own browser and logs each bed's sowing dates.
companion.limits: Logs what Ren reads out. Ren checks the entry.

companion.name: Bisi
companion.job: Drafts the weekly flower-share note from what Kemi texts it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Kemi sends the note.

popup.title: A parcel by the porch column
popup.body: A parcel leans against the white porch column. Ren carries it through the entry and the dining room to the shelf in the living room.

popup.title: Four things in the parcel
popup.body: Kemi unpacks the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. The footprint is about three quarters of a sheet of paper.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: While Haru naps, Ren plugs in the cable and presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Kemi joins from her phone
popup.body: Kemi joins the Core's own network from her phone. She picks the home network from the list and enters its password.

popup.title: Pick your first agents and apps
popup.body: In Companion Hub, Ren picks OpenClaw and Kemi picks Hermes. They add HortusFox, NocoDB and Listmonk, then go to make tea.

beats.capability: talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Bisi says good morning
popup.body: Kemi texts the agent she named Bisi. Bisi replies, and the Core is running.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: kemi
say.text: Morning, Kemi. Bisi here. Your move.

beats.capability: turn a database into a spreadsheet-style app without writing code

popup.title: Every subscriber is a row
popup.body: Before dawn, Ren opens the order sheet in NocoDB at the counter. Each flower-share subscriber is a row, and he ticks off the bunches as they are cut.

beats.capability: talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Bisi drafts the flower-share note
popup.body: Kemi texts Bisi this week's blooms. Bisi drafts the subscriber note. Kemi reads it and sends it from Listmonk herself.

say.speaker: kemi
say.text: Draft ready. Please read it before you send it.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals, notes and contacts

popup.title: The week's dinners, planned
popup.body: Kemi plans the week's dinners in Yuvomi at the range. The shopping list sits in the same app, so Ren shops from his phone.

beats.capability: track your plants, watering and care history across rooms and beds, with photos and a garden journal

popup.title: Hana logs the sowing dates
popup.body: Ren reads out the dahlia bed's sowing dates. Hana opens HortusFox in its own browser and logs each one. Ren checks the entry.

say.speaker: ren
say.text: Dates logged. Please check the entry.

beats.capability: resize and compress images in the browser; nothing is uploaded

popup.title: Bouquet photos, shrunk to fit
popup.body: On the deck, Kemi shrinks the morning's bouquet photos in Mazanoke so they fit the flower-share note. Nothing is uploaded.

beats.capability: design and prototype in a web-based design tool you host

popup.title: A label drawn at home
popup.body: Kemi lays out the new flower-share label in Penpot, a design tool hosted on the Core. She works in the glass nook, beside the beds.

beats.capability: your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices

popup.title: Client files, synced from the nook
popup.body: Kemi keeps her design clients' files in Nextcloud on the Core. The nook laptop and her phone sync the same folders.

beats.capability: a small CalDAV and CardDAV server for your calendars and contacts

popup.title: One calendar for stall days
popup.body: Ren and Kemi share the market calendar in Baikal: stall days, delivery days and wedding dates. Both phones read the same calendar.

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos on your own Core

popup.title: Haru's first year, kept here
popup.body: Ren adds Haru's ten-month photos to Immich beside the crib. The first-year album grows on the Core, next to the flower pictures.

beats.capability: keep customers, deals and custom fields in a CRM you host yourself

popup.title: A wedding enquiry, logged
popup.body: A wedding planner asks for September bunches. Ren adds the enquiry to Twenty at the dining table, with her color list.

beats.capability: send invoices and quotes, track expenses and time

popup.title: The quote, checked against orders
popup.body: Kemi writes the wedding quote in Invoice Ninja. Ren checks the bunches against the order sheet before it is sent.

beats.capability: stream your own music collection to any device

popup.title: A lullaby folder on the couch
popup.body: As Haru drifts off, Kemi plays the lullaby folder from Navidrome on her phone. It streams from the Core, and the room goes quiet.

beats.capability: a spreadsheet-database with real Python formulas, stored as a SQLite file you can copy

popup.title: The week's takings, added up
popup.body: By the fire, Ren totals the week's stall takings in Grist. Its formulas add up each market day, and the table is a SQLite file he can copy.

beats.capability: back up your files with encryption before they leave your Core

popup.title: A copy on a local disk
popup.body: Ren points Duplicati at a local disk beside the Core. It backs up the order sheet and Haru's photos, with encryption before they leave the Core.

beats.capability: watch your sites and services and get an alert when one goes down

popup.title: A status page for the farm
popup.body: Ren adds the order sheet and the photo library to Uptime Kuma. If either goes down, it alerts him.

beats.capability: translate text and documents on your own Core

popup.title: A reply for Ren's mother
popup.body: Kemi writes a reply to Ren's mother in English. LibreTranslate turns it into Japanese on the Core, and Ren checks the wording before it goes.

popup.title: One Core, one shelf, one farm
popup.body: A grower, a designer and a baby, with a farm to run. The Nakamura-Oduya family keeps it on one Companion Core in the living room.

closing.body: Your orders, your photos and your seasons can live on a Companion Core at home. Start with one order sheet in NocoDB.

notes: Owner sign-off open: the FTUE hotspot flow is written as the owner specified and is not on the fact sheet (STORY-BIBLE section 15, item 1).

No TV in this home: the media beat is Navidrome at the couch and the text never says TV or screen. The Core stands on the living room shelf; there is no desk, so office beats use room:office (the Garden Nook) with the couch as fallback.
living-watch is the iot beat: Uptime Kuma carries the catalog's IoT tag and watches services on the Core. Home Assistant was dropped because the fleet is over its cap. It makes no uptime promise.
living-backup: Duplicati's catalog caveat says name a local disk, which the text does. The words "with encryption before they leave the Core" copy the listing; no stronger security claim is made.
deck-card: LibreTranslate turns the reply into Japanese; check that Japanese is among the language models a Core installs (Yoruba was deliberately not used). Ren, not the app, confirms the wording.
kitchen-note: Listmonk needs an SMTP provider to send at volume (catalog caveat); the text claims no delivery. HortusFox runs under OpenClaw's own browser on the Core, so no website note is needed.
Voice-over lexicon: Nakamura, Oduya, Ren, Kemi, Haru, Hana, Bisi, Whistling Flat, HortusFox, NocoDB, Listmonk, Mazanoke, Penpot, Duplicati, LibreTranslate, Navidrome, Grist.
Street Orchard Moth Road and town Whistling Flat are invented; the human map check is still open.
